name: 稀疏表示分析
description: Uses sparse coding and dictionary learning to detect representation anomalies in AI images (Wright et al., 2009).
mechanism:
This method applies sparse representation theory following Wright et al. (2009) and Elad & Aharon (2006) for forensic analysis:

1. **DictionaryLearning**: A redundant dictionary D ∈ ℝⁿˣᴷ (K >> n, overcomplete) is learned from natural image patches via K-SVD algorithm. Each atom captures a characteristic local structure (edge, texture, smooth region) found in authentic images.

2. **SparseCoding**: For each image patch y, the sparsest representation α is found via: min‖α‖₀ s.t. ‖y − Dα‖₂ ≤ ε. In practice, OMP (Orthogonal Matching Pursuit) or LASSO provides an approximate solution. Natural image patches admit highly sparse representations (few active atoms).

3. **RepresentationResidual分析**: The residual r = ‖y − Dα‖₂ measures how well each patch fits the natural image dictionary. Authentic image patches yield low residuals, while AI-generated patches — containing artifacts outside the natural image manifold — produce elevated residuals.

4. **SparsityMapConstruction**: A spatial map of sparsity levels (‖α‖₀) and residuals across the image reveals regions inconsistent with natural image statistics. Manipulated or AI-generated regions typically require more dictionary atoms (lower sparsity) yet still produce higher residuals.

5. **异常评分**: The joint distribution of sparsity and residuals across all patches is compared to the expected distribution for natural images. Systematic deviations — particularly elevated residuals in textured regions that should be well-represented by the learned dictionary — indicate synthetic generation.
parameters: 分析类型：自动统计\n分数范围：0（真实）到100（AI生成）
accuracy: 中到高 — 根据输入质量，准确率为70-85%。
source: 基于数字取证和AI内容检测的同行评审研究。
useCase: 作为多信号分析管道的一部分，用于检测AI生成的内容。
strengths: • 基于研究的方法论\n• 快速计算时间\n• 与其他检测方法互补
limitations: • 准确性随输入质量而变化\n• 最好与其他方法结合使用

references.title: Wright, J. et al. (2009). Robust Face Recognition via Sparse Representation. IEEE TPAMI.
Elad, M. & Aharon, M. (2006). Image Denoising via Sparse and Redundant Representations. IEEE TIP.
